title: Al-Fajr: the dawn and ten nights
hookLine: by the dawn and ten nights, taken as the first ten of Dhul Hijjah (89:1–2)

cards: Five in the morning has its own kind of quiet. The streetlights are still on. The birds start before the traffic does.
New parents know that hour, and early-shift workers, and anyone with a flight to catch, usually by accident.

For Muslims who pray, it's the start of the day on purpose: the first of the five daily prayers is named for that hour, and comes before the sun is up. Al-Fajr, the surah just before Al-Balad, opens by swearing by it.

teach.b: Surah eighty-nine opens, in Pickthall's words: By the Dawn And ten nights.
Fajr comes from a root for breaking open, bursting through; the Qur'an uses the same root in Surah seventeen for a spring gushing out of the ground. Dawn is the moment light breaks through the dark.

teach.h: THE FIRST PRAYER OF THE DAY.
teach.b: It's also the name of the first daily prayer, prayed in the gray light before sunrise, when many people are still asleep. And ten nights. Which ten?

The reading Ibn Kathir prefers, which he traces to Ibn Abbas, is the first ten nights of Dhul Hijjah, the month of the Hajj, the days leading up to the pilgrimage's high point and the feast of Eid al-Adha.
Others said the last ten nights of Ramadan, and some the first ten of Muharram. The text itself leaves it open.
Those who take the Dhul Hijjah reading point to a hadith in Bukhari: no good deeds done on other days are better than those done in these ten.
So those days are kept with extra fasting, giving, and saying Allahu akbar, even far from Mecca. Then more oaths: by the even and the odd, by the night as it moves on.

teach.h: AN OATH FOR SOMEONE WITH SENSE.
teach.b: And a question: is there not in this an oath for someone with sense? The word for sense, hijr, means something that holds you back, a check, like a wall. The oaths are for the person whose mind can stop and notice.
A dawn, some nights, a question: the first of four days with this surah.

how: Muslims pray fajr, the dawn prayer, in the first light before sunrise; in the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah many fast, give charity and say the takbir often, taking these as the ten nights of Surah 89.

practice: Picture the earliest dawn you can remember seeing: the gray, the first bird, the cool air, and watch the light arrive. If you pray, that's the time of fajr; if you don't, it's still worth seeing.
